subject: astronomy
title: Space Exploration Stretch
welcome_lead: Evaluate the costs, benefits and trade-offs of crewed and robotic missions.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy stretch: ethics, costs and benefits of space exploration.
final_note: Exam questions often ask you to evaluate — use evidence, not opinion.

concepts.def: Uncrewed spacecraft, usually a probe or rover.
NASA-led plan to return humans to the Moon.
Rocket whose stages return for reflight, lowering cost.
Technology developed for space, used on Earth.
Defunct satellites and fragments orbiting Earth.

walkthroughs.body_html: Crewed missions are adaptable and inspiring but expensive and risky. Robotic missions are cheaper, can endure long durations and harsh environments, but lack human intuition.
Benefits include scientific discoveries, weather and GPS satellites, technological spin-offs (medical imaging, materials), and inspiration. Costs include money, risk to astronauts and space debris.
Give both sides: at least one benefit (science, technology, inspiration) and one cost (money, risk, debris). Then write a brief justified conclusion linked to a specific mission like JWST or Artemis.

mcqs.q: Which NASA programme aims to return humans to the Moon?
Which is a typical benefit of space exploration?

numericals.q: In what year did the SpaceX Crew Dragon perform its first crewed orbital launch?

free_texts.q: What name is given to defunct satellites and fragments orbiting Earth?
